checks.title: Physical photon dispersion (FZ-12)
checks.claim: The finite seam-edge symbol describes intrinsic propagation of physical photons in the same declared sector and frame, with a scale constrained independently of detector observations.
checks.acceptance: Trace the same-operator, photon sector, calibration, frame and physical scale. State whether a positive lower scale bound exists; then quantify sensitivity or show why a null cannot exclude the branch. Read primary observations separately and enforce eligibility.

checks.title: Same-source gravity
checks.claim: A single source-law refinement supplies its own metric, proper radii, generalized entropy, physical stress, and conservation with a common normalization.
checks.acceptance: Map each required observable to a native readout or explicitly mark it supplied/missing. Test common-region matching and residual scaling against at least one control. A fitted metric or finite algebra alone is insufficient.

checks.title: Gauge group and matter
checks.claim: Actual source responses, rather than a supplied matter fixture, pick the global Standard Model gauge group and its matter representations.
checks.acceptance: Independently calculate the center kernel for the declared representations. Distinguish a Lie algebra, a quotient and physical source selection; identify any independent alternatives admitted by the same premises.

checks.title: Fixed capacity and dark energy (FZ-13)
checks.claim: The same source law predicts fixed global capacity with a physical density and conservation interpretation, rather than imposing it.
checks.acceptance: Reproduce the continuity argument, inventory external calibration and covariance/eligibility, and show what would distinguish this branch from Lambda-CDM. Do not score historical data under a future protocol.

checks.title: One joint realization
checks.claim: One fixed observer law simultaneously produces the linked physical observables under shared settings and one measurement map.
checks.acceptance: Build a dependency matrix with required interfaces, fitted quantities and unresolved links. Evaluate any obstruction only against a fixed admitted class; do not generalize a branch-specific failure.
